WF.Path.Title: Path
WF.Path.LineLevelsHint: How many CONSECUTIVE levels this character has maintained Walking the Line. 1 gives +1, then +2, +3, and +1d caps it. Straying from the Line breaks the streak: the bonus is lost, and the count starts again from 0 if they return.
WF.Path.LineBonusHint: Unlike the Righteous and Damned modifiers, which apply only to their own audience, the Walking-the-Line bonus applies when dealing with folks of ANY Path.
WF.Settings.FumbleTableHint: Weird Frontiers has three fumble charts — Melee, Ranged and Firearms — but the DCC system holds only ONE fumble table globally and weapons carry no per-weapon override, so an automated fumble roll can only use one of them. Choose the one this table uses most; the other two are in the Weird Frontiers Critical Hit & Fumble Charts compendium and can be rolled by hand. This setting applies to PLAYER CHARACTERS only and is global, so choose "Leave the DCC system's table" in a world that also runs plain DCC characters. NPC fumbles are not automated at all: the DCC system looks up a creature's fumble chart by its critical-hit table name and searches only its own core-book compendium and the world's tables, never a module's — so roll Weird Frontiers creature fumbles by hand from the compendium.
WF.Path.LineLostHint: This character has strayed from the Line, so the bonus is LOST, not paused — the modifier from their current Path applies instead. The progression only counts levels the Line was maintained unbroken, so set this back to 0; if they return to the Line it starts again at +1. The number is left for you to clear rather than wiped automatically, so that nudging the track does not destroy it.
WF.Grit.Label: Grit
WF.Grit.Hint: Current Grit. Spent by Fear; at 0 the character is subject to Madness.
WF.Grit.MaxHint: Effective maximum: starting total less permanent loss
WF.Grit.Retired: Permanent Grit has reached 0 — this character is retired.
WF.Dinero.Label: Dinero
WF.Dinero.Hint: Weird Frontiers money is US dollars, to the cent. This is the same field as Funds on the Equipment tab.
WF.FumbleDie.Label: Fumble Die
WF.FumbleDie.Broken: Managed automatically. Weird Frontiers keys the fumble die to class and level, but the DCC system recomputes it from equipped armor on every refresh — and Weird Frontiers has no armor. This module applies the correct die as an Active Effect, which takes precedence. The field is read-only because a typed value would be discarded; change your class or level and it follows.
WF.Grit.StartingTotalHint: The character's original starting Grit, fixed at creation: (Stamina + Personality) / 2, rounded down. It does NOT move when temporary ability points are spent — only permanent loss reduces it.
WF.Grit.SuggestHint: (Stamina + Personality) / 2 from the current scores. Set this once at character creation.
WF.Grit.PermanentLossHint: Permanent Grit lost to erosion. An adventure in which Grit reached 0 costs 1 permanent Grit.
WF.Path.TheLineHint: Walking the Line — the modifier applies to folks of ANY Path, and grows with each level maintained at the Line: +1 at 1st level, then +2, +3, and +1d. That progression is not tracked here yet; apply it by hand.
WF.Firearm.IsFirearmHint: Firearms always use the Firearms critical hit chart, whatever the damage type below.
WF.Firearm.CaliberHint: As printed — .44, .58, or '10-12 gauge' for shotguns.
WF.Firearm.ActionTypeHint: As printed — Single, Double, Single/Double, Lever, Muzzleloading Single, Breechloading Single. Only a SINGLE action gun can be fanned. Note this is what the weapon table's TYPE column means for a firearm; for melee and ranged weapons that same column is the S/B/P damage type instead.
WF.Firearm.AmmoHint: C&B (cap and ball), Cart. (cartridge), ML/C&B, ML/Flintlock, Pinfire Cart., Volcanic 'Rocketball', Paper Cart. Ammunition costs a flat $1 per box of 50, any caliber.
WF.Firearm.RofHint: Rate of fire as printed, e.g. 2, '1 or 2', or '2 (1)' for a LeMat's second barrel. A hard ceiling: a gun can never fire more bullets in a round than this, even with extra action dice.
WF.Firearm.LoadHint: How many bullets the gun holds. A string, because shotguns print '1 or 2'.
WF.Firearm.ReloadTimeHint: Stored exactly as printed in the book. The books define it as rounds per single bullet, but gloss '1/3' as 'one bullet every 3 rounds' — which would make '3' and '1/3' identical, and the table uses both. Unresolved; enter the printed value and adjudicate at the table.
WF.Firearm.ConcealHint: Modifier on a contested Intelligence check to hide the weapon. Ties go to the higher Luck.
WF.Firearm.YearHint: Year of introduction, as printed. Flavour and judge adjudication.
WF.Firearm.DamageTypeHint: Selects the critical hit chart for melee and ranged weapons. Weird Frontiers keys crit tables to damage type, not to class and level as DCC does. Firearms use the Firearms chart regardless.
WF.Firearm.NoteRange: Range uses the Range field on the Weapon tab, short/medium/long. In Weird Frontiers those bands are FLAT ATTACK MODIFIERS — short +1, medium 0, long -1 — not DCC's damage-affecting range categories.
WF.Firearm.NoteRof: Each shot after the first on the same action die takes a cumulative -1. Fanning the hammer is -1d per shot instead, except for a gunslinger, who takes the flat -1.
WF.Firearm.NoteReload: Reloading under fire needs a DC 10 Agility check each round.
WF.Firearm.NoteBandedDamage: Shotguns carry banded damage (d14/d10/d7 for short/medium/long). Record it in the Banded damage field above and keep a single valid formula in the Damage field — Foundry parses '/' as division. LeMat-style guns print a second barrel's profile in parentheses; there is no second-profile field yet.
WF.Firearm.NoteNotAutomated: NONE of this is automated yet. These fields are data for the compendium and for the judge; ROF limits, range modifiers, reloading and conceal are all applied by hand.
WF.Firearm.BandedDamageHint: The printed short/medium/long damage profile, e.g. d14/d10/d7 for a shotgun. Recorded here, NOT in the Damage field.
WF.Firearm.BandedDamageNote: Put a single valid formula (the short band) in the Weapon tab's Damage field.
WF.Firearm.DamageDivisionWarning: WARNING: the Damage field on the Weapon tab contains a '/'. Foundry reads that as DIVISION — 'd14/d10/d7' rolls as 1d14 divided by 1d10 divided by 1d7, totalling about 1, with no error. Put a single formula there and record the banded profile in the field above.
WF.Firearm.CanBeFanned: Single action — this gun can be fanned.
WF.Firearm.PriceHint: Price in dollars, as printed. DCC's own Value field is coin-based and unused in Weird Frontiers.
WF.Firearm.PriceTextHint: The price exactly as printed. Kept alongside the number because some entries carry meaning a number cannot — 'for pair', or a bare figure with no dollar sign.
WF.Firearm.SecondBarrelHint: A LeMat-style gun's second barrel, printed in parentheses — e.g. d10/d6/d4 for the LeMat Revolver's shotgun barrel. Its ROF and load are likewise the parenthesised figures. Not automated.
WF.Firearm.MeleeNoteHint: Some guns double as hand weapons — Reid's Knuckleduster does d4 melee, the Dolne Apache d5 with brass knuckles or d4 with its blade.

WF.Class.LevelUpNote: Crit die, action dice, saves and titles all come from the class level-data compendium when you level up. Your signature die and tracks are shown above.
WF.Class.PercentTrackHint: A percentage track from your class progression chart — roll d% against it at each level.
WF.Tokens.BoonsHint: Boon tokens. Earned on a natural 20 — or a natural 1 on a roll where lower is better. Spend one for +1d to attack and damage on an attack, an instant Gun Deck reshuffle, clearing a Hex 1:1, a reroll (never a fumble), +1d or -1d on any roll, or +1d to an ally's next action. Not awarded automatically: the reversal depends on what the roll was for.
WF.Tokens.HexesHint: Hex tokens. Earned on a natural 1 — or a natural 20 on a roll where lower is better. They accumulate and stack; a Boon clears one. Not awarded automatically.
WF.Tokens.HexEffectsHint: None of these are applied automatically — they are the modifiers to apply by hand while you hold Hex tokens.
WF.ZeroLevel.Name: Frontier Folk (0-level)
WF.Dinero.EditOnCharacterTab: Dinero is edited on the Character tab.
WF.Npc.PathHint: Path of the Damned / Walking the Line / Path of the Righteous, as printed in the stat block. Replaces DCC's alignment.
WF.Npc.CritDieHint: Derived from Hit Dice, not stored — a tougher creature crits harder.
WF.Npc.FumbleDieHint: Derived from Hit Dice, not stored — a tougher creature fumbles less badly.
WF.Npc.CritTableHint: Weird Frontiers picks the crit table by attack type, where DCC uses a numeral by class and level.
WF.GunDeck.NaturalOneBody: The Gun deck card was safe, so this is not a misfire — the attack simply misses and no fumble is rolled.
WF.GunDeck.GunsmithFailed: Gunsmithy check of {total} fails the DC 5 — no misfire cards removed.
WF.GunDeck.GunsmithRemoved: Gunsmithy check of {total} — {n} misfire card(s) pulled from the deck before shuffling.
WF.GunDeck.MisfiresLeft: {n} aces and eights left in a deck of {size}.
WF.GunDeck.Reshuffle.cleaning: Cleaning my gun(s) — the deck is reshuffled.
WF.GunDeck.Reshuffle.boon: A Boon is spent for an instant reshuffle.
WF.GunDeck.NoBoon: No Boon tokens to spend. Reshuffling at any point during play costs a Boon; cleaning your guns during downtime is free.
WF.GunDeck.NeedsGM: A Gun deck has to be created by the Judge, and no GM is connected. Ask your Judge to log in, or to open your character's deck once.
WF.GunDeck.CreateTimeout: Timed out waiting for the Judge's client to create the Gun deck.
WF.Settings.DeckScopeHint: Who gets a Gun deck. One per character is the default — "one deck be used for all the character's firearms". Choose one per player for a funnel session, where a player running four characters would otherwise be shuffling four decks. Every NPC always shares a single Judge's deck, as the rules ask, rather than one deck per enemy.
WF.GunDeck.Title: Gun Deck — {n} shot(s)
WF.GunDeck.TitleFanning: Gun Deck — fanning the hammer, {n} shot(s)
WF.GunDeck.TookWorse: took the worse of two — also flipped {cards}
WF.GunDeck.FanningNote: Fanning needs a single-action pistol and a free hand, may exceed the gun's ROF, and a critical success is only possible on a d20 or larger die.
WF.GunDeck.DrawTwoNote: Two cards were flipped per shot and the worse result taken. Both cards leave the deck.
WF.GunDeck.Reshuffled: The last card was flipped, so the deck was reshuffled.
WF.GunDeck.Bonus: {n} to attack and damage, this shot only
WF.GunDeck.Result.inert: No effect — roll the ranged attack normally.
WF.GunDeck.Result.deadMansHand: Aces and eights — a dead man's hand.
WF.GunDeck.Result.redJoker: Lady Luck is keeping an eye on ya!
WF.GunDeck.Result.blackJoker: Lady Calamity is giving you the stinkeye!
WF.GunDeck.GhostIronJam: the round goes inert — a round to clear the jam
WF.GunDeck.GhostIronNote: Ghost-iron: the misfire stands but the Fumble chart is NOT rolled — the draw is treated as a misfire result instead. A Luck point may be spent to ignore the misfire.
WF.GunDeck.FumbleNote: Roll {formula} on the Firearm Fumble chart — the fumble die modified by the reverse of Luck.
WF.GunDeck.FumbleException: Not rolled automatically: if the attack roll was a critical success, the misfire still stands but the fumble is NOT rolled.
WF.GunDeck.CritNote: Roll on Crit Table Firearms for the automatic critical hit.
WF.Npc.GritDcHint: DC 8 + the creature's Hit Dice, plus any Hex tokens on the character making the check — that last part depends on who is looking, so it is not shown here.
WF.Sheet.SpecialAbilitiesHint: The published sheet has no class-specific boxes anywhere on it — every class ability, spell and knack is free text here.
WF.Sheet.TrailNotesHint: Page 2 of the published sheet: whatever the trail turns up.
WF.Sheet.ValuablesHint: Things worth money that are not dinero. Priced goods belong in the Goods list.
WF.Sheet.ArcaneVaultHint: Page 2 of the published sheet: relics, charms and whatever should not be handled bare-handed.
WF.Sheet.StableHint: Mounts. Horses are priced in the Goods compendium — Horse (average) $60, Horse (riding-good) $150.
WF.Sheet.SignatureHint: The published sheet prints five ruled rows here. These are derived from the weapons you have starred in the weapons list, so the numbers can never disagree with the item.
WF.Sheet.SignatureEmpty: No signature weapons. Star a weapon in the weapons list to list it here.
WF.Sheet.SignatureOverflow: The published sheet has room for {rows}; {count} more are starred.
WF.Sheet.SignatureToggle: Signature weapon — show this in the Signature Weapons block
WF.Fear.Outcome.success: Unfazed — the check matched or beat the DC.
WF.Fear.Outcome.criticalSuccess: Critical success on a natural 20 — a reaffirmation of faith.
WF.Fear.Outcome.failure: Failure — they succumb to the effects of fear.
WF.Fear.Outcome.criticalFailure: Critical failure on a natural 1 — a deeply seeded fear is struck.
WF.Fear.FearIndex: Fear chart index {index} — failed by {margin}, Luck {luckMod}, {hexes} Hex token(s).
WF.Fear.MadnessLine: Grit reached zero. Madness roll {total} ({modifier} from Luck and Hexes).
WF.Fear.NoRow: No row matched that total — the table may have been replaced or narrowed. Judge, please adjudicate.
WF.Fear.NoteImmune: No further Grit checks against {source} for the rest of the adventure, unless it presents itself in a new light.
WF.Fear.NoteCritSuccessBonus: +1d to attack rolls and spell checks against the source of fear for the rest of the encounter. Not applied — apply it by hand.
WF.Fear.NoteCritFailureAttacks: The source gains +1d to all attack rolls against this character for the rest of the encounter. Not applied — apply it by hand.
WF.Fear.NoteMadnessPenalty: −1d to all rolls for the remainder of the encounter. Not applied — apply it by hand.
WF.Fear.NoteAfflictionIsJudges: The specific phobia or disorder is chosen by the judge and player, never rolled. Check it will not cause real-world stress to anyone at the table.
WF.Fear.NoteErosionPending: Zero Grit was reached this adventure: 1 point of Grit is permanently lost when the adventure ends. Run the end-of-adventure recovery then, not now.
WF.Fear.Recovered: Grit restored to {after} of a starting {startingTotal}.
WF.Fear.RecoveredEroded: Grit reached zero this adventure, so 1 point is permanently lost: restored to {after}, with {permanentLoss} permanently eroded from a starting {startingTotal}.
WF.Fear.Retired: Permanent Grit has reached zero. This character has gone insane and is unfit for play — keep them in the story as an NPC.
WF.Fear.NoteBoonEarned: The natural 20 also earns a Boon. Not awarded — Boons and Hexes are manual counters in this module.
WF.Fear.NoteHexEarned: The natural 1 also earns a Hex. Not awarded — Boons and Hexes are manual counters in this module.
WF.Combat.Conceal.tie: A tie on both the roll and Luck. The book gives one tiebreak and this is past it — judge’s call.
WF.Combat.ConcealByLuck: The rolls tied, so the higher Luck score decided it.
WF.Combat.OutOfRange: Beyond long range. The book gives no modifier past the third band — judge’s call.
WF.Combat.OverRof: That is {overBy} shot(s) past this gun’s rate of fire ({ceiling}). Only fanning the hammer may exceed it.
